newsitem.title: USA: Bond dealers urge "measured" flow control approach.
newsitem.headline: Bond dealers urge "measured" flow control approach.

text.p: Municipal bond dealers urged a key U.S. Senate panel on Wednesday to pass "measured" flow control legislation that would protect only those localities with bond financed sites in operation at the time of the U.S. Surpreme Court's Carbone decision.
Flow control refers to the ability of local governments to require that municipal solid waste generated within their borders be processed at a designated site.
In a 1994 ruling in C.A. Carbone Inc. v. Town of Clarkstown, N.Y., the High Court struck down flow control as unconstitutional.
The U.S. Congress has tried unsuccessfully since the ruling to adopt a bill that would excuse, or "grandfather," many waste sites nationwide.
The Senate Committee on Environment and Public Works heard testimony from members of Congress and from localities on the issue earlier this week.
Some witnesses opposed any extension of flow control authority to local governments, while others said some "grandfathering" is imperative.
PSA, the bond market trade association, said in testimony submitted for the committee record on Wednesday that it backs a bare-bones approach to grandfathering sites.
"Congress has an obligation to provide affected localities with very limited flow control authority," the group said.

"Those who are facing serious problems as a result of the Supreme Court's actions (should be given enough time to) end the practice of flow control in a managed and orderly way," the group said in a four-page statement.
"After that, we recognize fully that all flow control authority would end forever," PSA said.

PSA said it had backed a broader bill last year that would have permitted some local governments that did not have bonds outstanding and that were not yet practicing flow control to practice it in the future.
But given the "current climate," PSA said, only a "more measured" approach is likely to win congressional approval this year.
